Prevention: Protect natural enemies such as spiders, dragon flies, ladybird beetles, predatory wasps and parasitic wasps through conservation of patches of natural vegetation.
Km) from other orchards that may be infested to prevent the flies crossing over.
Encourage fellow farmers to control fruit flies (area wide approach to fruit flies).
Remove neglected (unmanaged) host plants like guava, chillies, citrus, melons, coffee, mangoes, wild fruits to reduce pest population.
Use mulch and do not destroy long flowering weeds to attract natural enemies.
Harvest early when crop is mature and green because over- ripened fruits attract fruit flies.
Monitoring: Set pheromone traps to detect adult fruit flies presence.
Look for oviposition marks especially on immature fallen fruits.
Dissect the fruits with symptoms and examine them for larvae presence and fruit rot.
Look on fruit surfaces for small holes, punctured fruit, black lesions, soft spots, rotting, maggots and discolouration.
Look for pupae 2-5 cm beneath soil under host plant and take action to control as soon as fruit flies and damage symptoms are observed.
Direct Control: Increase pheromone traps density to 2-4 traps per acre depending on fruit flies infestation levels.
Trap flies using commercial pheromone traps - Methyl

Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
